purpose:
This report sets
out the Leaderâs recommended response on behalf of the City
Council to the letter from the Ministry of Housing, Communities and
Local Government (MHCLG) dated 19 May 2026.  The letter requested an
informal response from each authority in Lancashire regarding the

purpose:
A package of enabling work is well underway on
the Amounderness House Project, via a ‘JCT Minor Works
Building Contract with Contractors Design 2024’ between the
Council and the Contractor. The report seeks the Chief
Executive’s agreement to extend the existing contract to
allow further work to be undertaken (including the advanced placing
of orders of specific packages of further work) and would extend
the programme to the end of April 2026. The decision is required to
maintain programme momentum as getting into the main building works
contract is delayed.?
content:
Decision Taken
 
Resolved – That he Chief
Executive, following
consultation with the
Leader and Cabinet Member
for Resources, approves extending the ‘JCT Minor Works Building Contract with Contractors
Design’ for a further package of enabling
works and advanced placing of orders, amounting to
a total cumulative value which is set out in paragraph
3.4 of the report.
 

Reasons For Decision  
 
The reason for the decision is to ensure continuity of the enabling and
building works, in order
to maintain programme
momentum and to
avoid potential further costs.  This is a key transformational investment in
a Council owned
Grade ll building to provide a quality workspace
facility and
therefore if the works are
not progressed, this key
asset may not be developed, and
the Towns Fund
grant will not be effectively
utilised.

 

Alternative Options
Considered And Rejected

 

Not to extend the minor works
contract - this option has been rejected as it
could lead to additional costs and serious delays
to the project.
topline: The Chief Executive has decided to extend the 'JCT Minor Works Building Contract' for further enabling works and advanced orders.

purpose:
The Council was awarded £20m of
Levelling Up Fund (LUF) grant, as part of an overall £24.1m
LUF programme (‘Active Preston’), in 2023 to deliver a
range of major investments in active travel, parks and sport
provision. Two of the key projects being delivered under the LUF
Programme are the Moor Park and Waverley Park Projects.

The Parks projects have progressed to an advanced design stage and
are now ready to move into the main works contract stage. This
report therefore requests approval from the Chief Executive to (1)
approve the LRRP Stage 2 reports for the Moor Park and Waverley
Park projects (following consultation with the Leader &
Portfolio Holder) and (2) to enter into New Engineering Contract
(NEC4 Option A) for the delivery of main works.
content:
Decision Taken
 
That the ChiefExecutive
 
(i) approved,
following consultation with the Leader and Cabinet Member for
Community Wealth Building, the Stage 2 reports for the Moor Park
and Waverley Park projects.
 
(ii) approved entering
into New Engineering Contracts (NEC4 option A) with EWCE to
deliver the improvement works to Moor Park and Waverley Park for
the contract sums set out in paragraphs 3.19 and 3.21 of the
report.
 
Reasons For Decision
 
To ensure the engineering construction
contracts are in place for the delivery of the Moor Park and
Waverley Park improvement works within the programme
timescales.
 
Alternative Options
Consideredand Rejected
 
Not to enter into
these legal contracts would mean the delivery of the parks projects are put at significant risk and the Council could lose significant sums of
government funding.
topline: The Chief Executive has decided to approve Stage 2 reports and enter into engineering contracts for Moor Park and Waverley Park projects.

purpose:
The Council is currently using a version of
Income Management for the telephone payment system that is no
longer compliant with the Payment Card Industry Data Security
Standard (PCI DSS). PCI DSS is a set of security standards designed
to ensure that all companies that accept, process, store, or
transmit debit/credit card information maintain a secure
environment.

A change in latest version of the PCI DSS means that it is no
longer permissible for a customer to speak their credit card
information over the telephone to a Customer Advisor as this is
considered insecure. Alternative secure methods must be implemented
for the Council to become PCI-DSS compliant and for our income

Standard (PCI DSS). PCI DSS is a set of security standards designed
to ensure that all companies that accept, process, store, or
transmit debit/credit card information maintain a secure
environment.

purpose:
The Revenues & Benefits shared service
currently utilises an e-billing platform provided by Publisure who
we have worked with for a long time. Publisure sits in between the
Council and our external mailing house AdareSEC. As well as
providing our current e-billing platform, Publisure also provides
software that allows user friendly templates and consolidates post
across all services before sending a print file to AdareSEC who
then print and send the letters.

Attempts to increase the number of e-billing service users have
been made over the years, however, take up has been low as the
current system is quite cumbersome – relying on the use of a
PIN number to access correspondence. At annual billing time and
throughout the year, the admin team are inundated with requests for
reminders of forgotten PIN numbers. The current system is also
admin heavy in terms of setting up users as this is a back-office
manual process.
content:
Resolved
– That the Cabinet Member for Resources approved the Council
entering into a three year contract with Publisure at a total cost
of £48,300, for the delivery of an enhanced e-billing
system.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Resources has decided to approve a three year contract with Publisure for an enhanced e-billing system.

purpose:
Amounderness House is a key project being
delivered by the Council under the Towns Fund Investment Programme
under the ‘Renewal of Harris Quarter Assets’ scheme and
involves the refurbishment and conversion of the heritage building
into a managed office facility. There have been several reports to
Council over the last few years, the most recent report in December
2024.

The report set out the latest overall cost position on the
Amounderness House project and seeks an additional increase in the
project’s budget, under delegated decision powers to the
Cabinet Member.
content:
Decision Taken
 
That the Cabinet Member for Resources
 
 

(i)        
Approved a virement of
an additional sum from the capital programme scheme as set out
within section 4.13, thereby increasing the Council’s total
funding contribution as set out in para 3.8 of the
report.
 

(ii)       
Noted the revised
overall budget for the Amounderness
House scheme as set out within para 3.8 of the
report. 

 
 
Reason for
Decision
 
This increase in the net funding contribution
from the Council and associated increase in the project’s
budget will enable the scheme to be progressed and enable it to be
delivered within the timescales for the Towns Fund
Programme.  The building’s
transformation will make a significant new contribution to the City
Centre offer, support the small business sector and growing
experience economy. It will make the City Centre more desirable as
a place to visit, spend time, work and live.
 
Alternatives
Considered and Rejected
 

Option 1 – Do Nothing

         

         
This was rejected.  If the scheme was
not brought forward within these timescales, then, the cost would
increase further as the contractor will not hold its prices, and
the external 
Towns Fund grant could be affected.

 

         

Option 2

         

          Do
not secure the additional Council funding - This was rejected as
this would mean that the scheme design would require further
changes which would delay the scheme further.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Resources has decided to approve additional funding for the Amounderness House scheme to enhance the City Centre offer and support the small business sector.
